findings.current: A small explosion sounded somewhere deep inside the mollusk’s glistening body.
findings.defect: The draft relocates the explosion from deep beneath the Kraken’s wet, glistening skin to an unspecified place inside its entire body.
findings.rationale: 피부 깊숙한 specifies a location deep beneath or within the skin, while 몸 전체에 해당하는 “body” is broader.
findings.replacement: A small explosion sounded somewhere deep beneath the mollusk’s wet, glistening skin.
findings.source: 물기로 번들거리는 연체동물의 피부 깊숙한 어느 곳에서 작은 폭발음이 들렸다.

findings.current: The existence of the powerful Kraken, despite being merely a named monster.
findings.defect: “Merely a named monster” incorrectly makes the named-monster classification sound unimpressive. The source treats the Kraken’s strength as exceptional even with its named-monster status taken into account.
findings.rationale: 제아무리 …라고는 하나 concedes the Kraken’s named-monster status before emphasizing how strikingly powerful it is.
findings.replacement: The existence of a Kraken this powerful, even for a named monster.
findings.source: 제아무리 네임드 몬스터라고는 하나, 강력한 힘을 지닌 크라켄의 존재.

findings.current: And the involvement of someone else, which the Kraken had confessed to itself.
findings.defect: The placement of “itself” says that the Kraken confessed the information to itself rather than that the Kraken itself made the admission.
findings.rationale: 스스로 modifies the Kraken as the party making the admission; it does not identify the recipient of a confession.
findings.replacement: And the involvement of someone else, which the Kraken itself had admitted.
findings.source: 그리고 크라켄이 스스로 실토한 또 다른 누군가의 개입.

findings.current: The moment I heard those two words—*human*—a chilling cold shot up my spine.
findings.defect: “Human” is one English word, so calling it “two words” is internally incorrect. 두 글자 refers to the two Korean syllabic characters of 인간.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the source’s focus on the two-part sound of 인간 without making a false claim about the English word count.
findings.replacement: The moment I heard that two-syllable word—*human*—a chilling cold shot up my spine.
findings.source: 인간. 그 두 글자를 듣는 순간, 몸서리쳐질 만큼 차가운 한기가 등골을 타고 솟구쳤다.

findings.current: It had to die. I wanted it dead.
findings.defect: The draft changes the repeated necessity to kill the Kraken into a statement of desire, weakening the deliberate repetition and Taekyung’s moral certainty.
findings.rationale: Both clauses repeat 죽여야, expressing obligation or necessity rather than merely wanting the Kraken dead.
findings.replacement: I had to kill it. I had to.

findings.current: I drew up Scorching Yang Qi, which was practically the opposite of poison, while putting on the Myriad-Poison Ring I had taken from my inventory.
findings.defect: “The opposite of poison” is an unnatural and mechanically vague rendering of 상극, which means that the qi counteracts poison.
findings.rationale: 상극 describes forces that oppose or counteract each other; here it explains why Scorching Yang Qi can help expel the poison.
findings.replacement: I drew up Scorching Yang Qi, which countered poison, while putting on the Myriad-Poison Ring I had taken from my inventory.
findings.source: 나는 독에 상극이라 할 수 있는 열양지기를 끌어올림과 동시에, 인벤토리에서 꺼낸 만독지환을 착용했다.

summary: Six actionable findings: two meaningful distortions of Taekyung’s reasoning, one incorrect grammatical attachment, and three localized fidelity or wording issues.
